cor.heading: Inventory and Cost of Goods Sold
cor.text: We consider our estimates of obsolete or slow-moving inventory and shrinkage in determining the appropriate overall valuation allowance for inventory. We monitor our sales margins for each type of inventory on an ongoing basis and compare to historical margins. Significant variances in those margins may require a revision to future inventory reserve estimates. We have historically revised our reserve pertaining to jewelry inventory depending on the current price of gold and resulting trends in margins. Future declines in gold prices may cause an increase in reserve rates pertaining to jewelry inventory. As of September 30, 2025, the gross balance of our inventory was $252.0 million, for which we have included reserves of $3.6 million. Assuming the reserve rates were increased or decreased by 10%, our inventory reserve balance as of September 30, 2025 would have increased or decreased by approximately $0.4 million.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text:
Management believes that it is more likely than not that forecasted income, including income that may be generated as a result of certain tax planning strategies, together with future reversals of existing taxable temporary differences, will be sufficient to fully recover the net recorded deferred tax assets. In the event we determine all or part of the net deferred tax assets are not realizable in the future, we will make an adjustment to the valuation allowance that would be charged to earnings in the period such determination is made. We have included valuation allowances against deferred tax assets for net operating losses and tax credits not expected to be utilized based on specific facts and estimates for each jurisdiction.

We consider the earnings of certain non-U.S. subsidiaries to be indefinitely invested outside the U.S. on the basis of estimates that future domestic cash generation will be sufficient to meet future domestic cash needs and our specific plans for reinvestment of those subsidiary earnings. We have not recorded a deferred tax liability related to foreign withholding taxes of our undistributed earnings of foreign subsidiaries indefinitely invested outside the U.S.

We may be subject to income tax audits by the respective tax authorities in any or all of the jurisdictions in which we operate or have operated within a relevant period.

As of September 30, 2025, the balance of our PSC receivable was $48.7 million. Assuming the average forfeiture rate increased or decreased by 10%, our pawn service charges receivable balance as of September 30, 2025 would have increased or decreased by approximately $1.5 million.

gp.text: Total revenues increased $420.4 million (33%) and gross profit increased 32%, reflecting improved PSC revenue, merchandise sales and jewelry scrap gross profit.

cor.heading: Inventory and Cost of Goods Sold
cor.text: We consider our estimates of obsolete or slow-moving inventory and shrinkage in determining the appropriate overall valuation allowance for inventory. We monitor our sales margins for each type of inventory on an ongoing basis and compare to historical margins. Significant variances in those margins may require a revision to future inventory reserve estimates. We have historically revised our reserve pertaining to jewelry inventory depending on the current price of gold and resulting trends in margins. Future declines in gold prices may cause an increase in reserve rates pertaining to jewelry inventory. As of September 30, 2026, the gross balance of our inventory was $361.8 million, for which we have included reserves of $3.5 million. Assuming the reserve rates were increased or decreased by 10%, our inventory reserve balance as of September 30, 2026 would have increased or decreased by approximately $0.4 million.

General and administrative expenses increased $27.2 million primarily due to increased labor costs (including higher incentive compensation) and expenses associated with SMG.

nonop.text: Total non-operating expense changed by $12.9 million, primarily due to the increase in interest expense of $10.8 million, which is a result of the issuance of the 2032 Senior Notes in the second quarter of fiscal 2025.

pretax.text: Income tax expense increased $20.6 million, primarily due to increased income before income taxes of $77.6 million. Income tax expense includes other items that do not necessarily correspond to pre-tax earnings and create volatility in our effective tax rate. These items include the net effect of state taxes, non-deductible items and changes in valuation allowances for certain foreign operations. See Note 10: Income Taxes of Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements included in “Part II, Item 8 — Financial Statements and Supplementary Data.”

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text:
Management believes that it is more likely than not that forecasted income, including income that may be generated as a result of certain tax planning strategies, together with future reversals of existing taxable temporary differences, will be sufficient to fully recover the net recorded deferred tax assets. In the event we determine all or part of the net deferred tax assets are not realizable in the future, we will make an adjustment to the valuation allowance that would be charged to earnings in the period such determination is made. We have included valuation allowances against deferred tax assets for net operating losses and tax credits not expected to be utilized based on specific facts and estimates for each jurisdiction.

We consider the earnings of certain non-U.S. subsidiaries to be indefinitely invested outside the U.S. on the basis of estimates that future domestic cash generation will be sufficient to meet future domestic cash needs and our specific plans for reinvestment of those subsidiary earnings. We have not recorded a deferred tax liability related to foreign withholding taxes of our undistributed earnings of foreign subsidiaries indefinitely invested outside the U.S.

We may be subject to income tax audits by the respective tax authorities in any or all of the jurisdictions in which we operate or have operated within a relevant period.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

accounts.note: Depreciation and amortisation includes the amortisation of intangibles where the filing reports one line: the PP&E residual then carries the intangibles' share.

accounts.name: Goodwill and intangibles
accounts.note: Acquisitions add goodwill and intangibles at their allocated values, not at the cash paid; the residual is the difference and the amortisation.

accounts.name: Equity
accounts.note: Other comprehensive income (currency translation, unrealised gains) moves equity without passing through net income: it is in the residual.

s.t: In fiscal 2026, PSC accounted for approximately 35% of our total revenues and 61% of our gross profit.
As of September 30, 2026 , 62% of our U.S. stores were located in Texas (42%) and Florida (20%), and those stores account for a significant portion of our revenues and profitability.

The total assets, excluding goodwill and other identifiable intangibles, which are included within the scope of the assessment, and total revenues of Founders One, LLC excluded from management’s assessment represented 5% and 8% of the Company’s consolidated total assets and consolidated total revenues, respectively, as of and for the year ended September 30, 2026.

Total assets (excluding goodwill and intangibles) and total revenues of Founders One, LLC constituted 5% and 8% of total assets and total revenues, respectively, as of and for the year ended September 30, 2026.

Total assets (excluding goodwill and intangibles) and total revenues of the 12 pawn stores in Texas constituted less than 1% each of total assets and total revenues as of and for the year ended September 30, 2026.
And we rely on six foundational capabilities to execute our strategy and achieve our purpose:
Thus, we do not maintain or rely on mass supply, distribution or warehousing facilities.
• Our store operations leave a relatively small carbon footprint when compared to big-box or other mass retailers that rely on manufacturers and extensive supply chain and distribution channels.

The success of our business depends on the efficiency and reliability of our information technology and business systems and related controls, including the point-of-sale system utilized in our store locations.

Our ability to obtain debt or equity financing, including the possible refinancing of existing indebtedness, will depend upon market conditions, our financial condition and the willingness of financing sources to make capital available to us at acceptable rates and terms.
We rely on third-party vendors for AI Technologies, and our business could be negatively impacted if the vendors or AI Technologies become unavailable, fail or are ineffective or otherwise flawed.
We rely on certain intellectual property and our inability to protect or defend our intellectual property rights could negatively affect our business and results of operations.
Jewelry scrap sales increased 100%, and jewelry scrap sales gross margin increased from 27% to 32% due to increase in gold price and jewelry purchases.
Aged general merchandise decreased below 1% of total general merchandise inventory.
Our primary sources of funds includes cash generated from operations and borrowings from the issuance of debt.
Assuming the reserve rates were increased or decreased by 10%, our inventory reserve balance as of September 30, 2026 would have increased or decreased by approximately $0.4 million.
The proceeds of scrap sales and our ability to sell jewelry inventory at an acceptable margin depend on gold values.
The controlling shareholder or the Board may implement changes in the future that would again require the Company to rely on the Controlled Company exemptions under the Nasdaq Listing Rules.

See Note 9: Common Stock and Stock Compensation of Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements included in “Part II, Item 8 — Financial Statements and Supplementary Data.” The actual value realized by the Named Executive Officer with respect to stock awards will depend on whether the award vests and, if it vests, the market value of our stock on the date the stock is sold.
The actual value realized by the director with respect to stock awards will depend on the market value of our stock on the date the stock is sold.

s.t: In fiscal 2022, we invested $ 15.0 million in exchange for a non-redeemable voting participating preferred equity interest in Founders, a then newly-formed entity with one other member.
In fiscal 2024, we contributed an additional $ 15.0 million associated with our preferred interest, bringing our total preferred equity investment in Founders to $ 45.0 million.

In prior periods, our preferred equity investment in Founders, a variable interest entity, was accounted for utilizing the measurement alternative within ASC 321, Investments — Equity Securities and presented in “Other investments” in our Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets.
In fiscal 2022, we invested $ 15.0 million in exchange for a non-redeemable voting participating preferred equity interest in Founders, a then newly-formed entity with one other member.
The total consideration transferred included, among other things, the exchange of the Company’s existing $45.0 million preferred equity investment into common equity of Founders.
In fiscal 2024, we contributed an additional $ 15.0 million associated with our preferred interest, bringing our total preferred equity investment in Founders to $ 45.0 million.

We account for our investment in Rich Data Corporation (“RDC”) using the measurement alternative in ASC 321, Investments — Equity Securities, to measure this investment at cost, less any impairment, plus or minus changes resulting from observable price changes in orderly transactions for identical or similar investments of the same issuer, if any.

Our ability to recover our investments in other companies (such as our investment in Rich Data Corporation) is heavily dependent on the success and performance of those companies, including their respective ability to obtain further debt or equity financing.

In the prior periods, our preferred equity investment in Founders, a variable interest entity, was accounted for utilizing the measurement alternative within ASC 321, Investments — Equity Securities and presented in “Other investments” in our Consolidated Balance Sheets.
